really look that desperate for a pet?

Alice lived in a place where it always snowed heavily.

Elysium?

Elysium.
A place without suffering and pain...
A happy place.

If the Ark was really an Elysium,
wouldn't a happy world exist in there?
My Queen,
is the Ark really an Elysium?

Well...
The Ark is a kind of Elysium...

Then the Ark really is Elysium!

Maybe the Heart Queen would not have to be defeated in order to find a happy world.

Not exactly.

Go and see it with your own eyes.
If that place is really Elysium.
If a happy world exists there.

... This world, verily, was once brimmed with life, and bountiful.
Do you miss the past?
... Men are, alas, frail and feeble of heart.
And in sooth,
Nikkes, who erst were mortal, are no less in this regard.
To yearn for days of yore...
To mourn that which hath been lost, and to crave its return...
Is this not the manner of men?
And yet...
And yet...?
... Heaven's mercy! I nigh let slip a careless word once more.
I pray thee, disregard my last utterance.
'Twas naught but a musing...
that a man's true nature changeth scarcely ever.
... Great Hero.
In what manner dost thou intend to contend with the Maleficent Beast Quartet?
I'll have a conversation with them.
A discourse...?
Yeah, I'll talk to them
and convince them to join our side.
Verily...
dost thou deem it feasible?
... I guess so.
Ho,
wherefore dost thou seek discourse?
Other ways there are aplenty.
The simplest perforce, of course, is to quell them by force.
With the might of those maidens at thy side,
'tis well within thy power to bring it about.
I'll do it if I need to.
We've already done it once before.
But for now... I'm keeping it as a last resort.
Wherefore?
To have the opposition submit ere discourse
is a stratagem oft employed,
and verily, a most efficacious one.
... You're not wrong,
but I don't think it'll turn out well in the long run. Also...
I don't think it's necessary to go all-out at the moment.
... Is that so?
That is thy way...
Nayuta resumes her slow gait.
Shall we tarry a while longer?
'Tis long since I last partook in such discourse, and verily, it doth gladden my heart.
... As she says that, Nayuta begins retracing her steps.
... I said I'd lead the way.
Q&A: Forbearance
Nayuta and I stroll slowly on top of Whaley.
Of thy reason I have heard.
Yet prithee, wherefore hast thou resolved
to hold discourse with the Maleficent Beast Quartet?
Well...
At Nayuta's question, I retrace my memories.
... Just because.
Heh... in sooth, sayest thou there be no cause?
I'd say it's more like...
I briefly explain to Nayuta what happened with the Four Beasts.
Actually, they were the ones who wanted to talk first.
They heard that conversation is the cornerstone of evolution.
A wise sentiment indeed.
By such pronouncements wert thou swayed?
Yeah...
but I thought it was the right thing to do.
To be precise, I thought I could persuade them.
Hmm...
... Methinks I do now perceive thee more clearly, Great Hero.
Oh? What do you think of me?
Thou art one who taketh pleasure in smiting maidens in jest,
and in making acquaintance with them beyond what need requireth.
That's not...
Rapi...!
Haha, wouldst thou deny it so?
Verily... ere I was aware, mine own heart had yielded itself unto thee.
... Why's that?
Hmm...
I deem it not begotten solely of the utterances of the other Forerunners.
Methinks...
'tis rather born of having beheld the speech and comportment of the maidens that do attend thee.
You mean Matis and Rapi?
So it is. Yet the other maidens are included, nonetheless.
Nayuta stops and turns to face me.
I, too, do possess some knowledge touching the history of the Ark,
and right well do I know how the Nikkes are entreated.
Oft hath mine eyes beheld
how those who name themselves commanders do deal with them.
When first I heard the tale from the Forerunner maidens,
I believed it not that one such as thee could verily exist.
Thus did I resolve to behold it with mine own eyes.
So... is that why you've been wandering around?
Haha. Not for that cause alone, though in part it was indeed so.
Huh?
Haha, my most humble apologies. 'Twas a slip of the tongue.
Aye...
'tis but one among many reasons, verily.
At any rate, to meet thee here atop the White Giant,
and share such words as these...
Verily, the workings of fate doth surpass all understanding.
Fate...
Verily,
betwixt thee and the maidens doth exist a bond most strong.
And such a bond doth stand as testament to the depth of thine affections for one another.
Having beheld this, I too do find myself, unawares, placing my trust in thee.
... Thanks.
Haha, I hath strayed from the path of our tale.
Yet, in sooth, the answer lieth in that
thou art a man of vast capacity.
Therefore... it is by reason thereof that thou art able to choose such a course.
Verily, thy approach doth stand as the true and rightful path.
Of this, at least, I remain most assured.
Yet...
Yet...?
Yet one cannot always take the righteous way.
To be righteous oft doth bring inefficiency.
And inefficiency doth...
maketh it more likely that thou shalt fail to attain thine aims.
Then, what if I try again...?
If there be no second chance...
and if the stake be this world itself...
then the matter differeth, doth it not?
What's your goal, Nayuta?
It differeth not from thee.
Yet my path... mayhap lies otherwise.
And what way would that be?
Methinks we have strayed far afield.
'Tis time we make our return.
As she says so, Nayuta walks toward Whaley's head...
Q&A: Crossroads
Oh...
By yielding myself unto the course of nature, I find myself returned hither.
Is it not most wondrous?
Well, that's because we went back the way we came...
Surely not.
This time, I had hoped to journey to a place mine eyes ne'er yet beheld.
Haha, what doth it matter?
As I spake but now,
to wander whither mine feet leadeth me is my role.
Well, our company goeth by the name of the Forerunners, is it not?
... Yeah, true that.
By the way, you said the Pioneers told you about me?
Aye.
Verily, I have beheld thee also.
You saw me?
'Tis one of Persinette's licentious paintings.
So wondrously lifelike the portrayal, that mine heart was ensnared unwittingly...
Can we please stop talking about the paintings?!
Hahaha.
Nayuta leans down to examine the vegetables growing in the garden.
Apart from the tale that thou and Scarlet did partake of compost,
I have verily heard many a tale of thee from the Forerunners.
... What'd they say about me?
Hmmm... how should I utter it... Ah, verily!
Nayuta averts her eyes from the vegetables and straightens up.
The Forerunners spake thus:
thou art one who goeth about sowing seeds.
Sowing seeds?
I-I told you to stop talking about the paintings...!
Hahaha. Nay, 'twas but a metaphor; such was not mine intent.
That's a metaphor too...?
Mine meaning is thus:
thou sowest seeds of hope for the morrow.
I am but a fool, and know not what thoughts dwell within thee.
Yet by the tales from the Forerunner maidens,
’tis plain thou dost prepare
for more than merely staying the Raptures' advance.
Well... we've got a lot to do.
First, we need to reclaim the surface. To do that, we'll have to fight the Raptures.
I think persuading the Four Beasts will help.
And then...
Speakest thou of Young Lady Marian?
You ever met her?
Nay, but the Forerunners have spoken of her, though but briefly.
They say... thou and she share a bond most tender.
... Yeah, something like that.
Ah... so it seems.
Why...? What's wrong?
Nay, 'tis of no great import.
I did but hope fortune might favor me.
Yet 'tis plain thy heart hath found another. Alas, my heart is sore cast down.
... You're terrible at skirting the truth, aren't you?
Was it apparent?
Nayuta clasps her hands behind her back and once again moves off somewhere.
Wait, where are you going...?
Ought we not now to make our return?
The others await us.
... It's that way.
I point in the exact opposite direction from where Nayuta is headed.
Ah, I had nigh lost my way once more.
... 'Tis most fortunate indeed that thou art here, Great Hero.
Come on, follow me.
Very well.
The Monk's Request
We walk for a bit and soon spot our companions waiting in the distance.
I thank thee for indulging my whims.
'Tis little enough to repay thee,
but hast aught thou wouldst inquire of me, Great Hero?
Hmm...
... So, how was your little test?
Do I seem trustworthy to you now?
Hahaha. Verily, thou art a man of great valor.
My paltry stratagem could not beguile thee.
... You didn't even try to hide it.
Aye, I would fain know the manner of person thou art.
And verily, thy answers to my queries
surpass all that I did imagine.
... I see.
Forsooth, to behold is to believe.
... Whereupon,
in turn, I shall ask thee once more:
What dost thou behold of this humble one?
To be honest... I still don't really know.
Haha. Then shalt thou, in time, come to know this humble one.
Verily, this matter hath forged a bond betwixt thee and me.
... All right, let's meet Leviathan and Ziz first, and then figure out what to do next.
That is indeed a most excellent notion.
Nayuta begins walking ahead toward the group.
... Great Hero.
In this brief discourse of ours,
knowest thou the moment I deemed most wondrous?
When was it?
'Twas naught but the moment when I, having strayed upon a wrong path,
was bidden to follow thee as thou walkedst ahead.
... Really?
Verily, thou knowest full well the heart of a maiden.
Uh... no...
Nayuta slows her pace slightly.
... Great Hero, should I misstep again,
perchance e'en in the farthest morrow,
I pray thee, guide my steps aright.
Sure thing.
Pray thee, ponder with greater diligence ere thou dost reply.
What if thou findest thyself astray on mine account?
Don't worry, I'm good with directions. And...
even if we do get lost, we can just wander around together.
So it is?
... I am greatly beholden.
Daresay, ne'er have words more comforting graced mine ears.
R-really?
M-maybe it's time you learned how to read a map.
Hahaha.
Nayuta laughs and leads the way.
I shall count on thee henceforth, Great Hero.
Aye...
be it whichever humble servant I am.
The King's Subjects
On the way to Red Hood's hometown,
Chime tells everyone to stop.
Let us tarry here but a moment.
I'm fine. Let's keep going.
Dost thou think thou wouldst still be well after walking so long without rest?
Rest when it is time to rest; thus shalt thou go the farther.
Let's do what she says and chill for a bit.
Even you, Commander, aren't made of steel, and we've been walking forever.
Yeah! You know what they say, haste makes waste!
I believe in Rapi!
Er... I mean, the Rapi inside this person called Red Hood!
Neon moves ahead and sees Red Hood and Dorothy sitting by the roadside, talking.
... Okay, fine.
Now then, I shall prepare but a simple morsel, that we may regain our strength.
*Clatter*
Chime pulls out what looks like camping gear.
Ye two, go yonder to that hillside and gather some branches.
Break none that are yet living, but only take those that lie fallen and dead.
You're gonna start a fire?
First Red Hood, and now you?
Am I gonna have to chew you out too for starting a fire?
Back then, were we not right in the very heart of a ruin, where Raptures could spring forth at any moment?
Chime points at our surroundings.
Hills flank the twisting road, bare trees dotting the slopes sparsely.
Those hills shall surely hide even the smoke of a bonfire.
And if we burn dead branches, not a wisp of smoke shall appear.
Hmm...
Fie! Make haste and do it; why so much wailing?
Had I erred, I had perished many a year ago!
... I guess you're right.
... Yeah, that's true.
... Can't argue with that.
And with the firepower we've got,
we can handle anything... as long as it's not the Rapture Queen.
'Tis right.
We've got two Nikkes from the Goddess Squad, too.
Fear not, for Her Highness is here.
Er...
Do you mean Crown?
Neon points at Crown,
who's sitting a little apart from us.
... She somehow looks a bit full of herself.
Her Highness is most mighty,
the mightiest in all the world!
... Uh-huh.
She's a Pilgrim, so of course she's strong... but—
Bah! Quibble not and be gone at once!
Canst thou not see that Her Highness is hungry?
I sneak another glance at Crown.
She's holding a knife and fork, drool trickling from the corner of her mouth...
... All right, I'll be right back.
Hold, Rapscallion. Thou shalt stay here and lend me a hand.
... Huh?
Did I not bid those two fetch the firewood?
Anis and Neon go off to gather firewood.
*Scrub scrub*
... Chime and I end up at a nearby water pipe, scrubbing the potatoes clean.
Scrub it harder!
Not a speck of dirt shall sully the potatoes which Her Highness doth eat.
... Got it.
Yeah, yeah.
How obedient art thou! I like it well.
Oi, Rapscallion! How darest thou speak so?!
... Chime.
*Scrub scrub*
What aileth thee?
Why are you making me do this all of a sudden?
*Plunk*
Chime drops the potato she'd been carefully washing.
She stares at me, disbelief written all over her face.
... Dost thou truly not know?
You...
... Rapscallion!
Thou knowest naught of what thou hast done?
Uh... no?
Thou hast the gall to refuse the post of advisor? How audacious!
Thou shouldst have been smitten by divine wrath,
yet by Her Highness's mercy thou art spared. Be grateful, Rapscallion!
I look back at Crown again...
It seems she's a bit upset...
Take it meekly!
Until this journey ends, thou art mine aide!
The Aide's Aide
Um, Anis?
Yeah?
So... what do you even call an aide's aide?
Dunno...
Aide... Aide...
... Ai-aide?
Heh.
Pfft!
What art thou waiting for! Hasten to help with Her Highness's meal!
Yes, ma'am...
And just like that, I'm now Chime's aide.
This potato's still half-raw!
Canst thou not even roast a simple potato?
Clean up the camp!
Cover the fire with earth and strew some leaves where thou didst sit!
Egads! What thinkest thou art doing?!
See to it that Her Highness is ready afore we set forth!
Just so you know, Commander, we're ready to roll!
Yep! We're good to go as soon as you're done, Master.
Don't just join in the teasing! Try to stop her...
Huh? Why should I?
Honestly, I think it's for the best if you stay active like this for a while.
Yeah, me too.
I don't know about that...
What art thou dawdling for, Rapscallion!
Oh dear! My apologies, Your Highness.
My aide's still a bumbling fool, I fear.
Shouldn't we head over now?
I'm going...
We set off again,
chatting as we follow Dorothy and Red Hood, who take the lead.
And beside me is...
The aide's poise reflecteth the master's own!
Straighten thy shoulders! Lift thy head!
Walk with pride, as befitteth one of noble station!
... Chime sticks to me, talking away without pause.
Hmm...
'Tis a rare occasion indeed to speak at such length; I shall therefore continue the tale of our kingdom, which I left unfinished ere this.
... Nay, that will not do. Given our present plight,
'twould be better to recount our treasure-hunting exploits instead.
Chime...
Be silent, for 'tis time I begin my tale.
... Why are you doing this to me?
Did I not bid thee be silent?!
Now then... where should I begin my tale... Ah, yes!
'Twas when I first ascended to the surface...
I knew she was cool,
but damn, she's way cooler than I thought!
Right?
She seems super thoughtful.
Hehe. The most dependable of all.
I am proud to call her my loyal aide.
Precious Ones, The Journey Continues
As we walk, Chime keeps telling her story.
So I did strike open the chest!
And wouldst thou believe it? 'Twas utterly empty!
Perchance another hath claimed it before us!
... Oh, right.
Hmm... that look is far more pleasing to mine eyes.
... Huh?
'Tis far better than that fretful, fidgety look from afore, I daresay.
Did I... look like that?
Indeed 'tis so.
Utterly dead-faced, and a trial to behold.
Ah... I see it now.
That Rapi fellow is as precious to thee
as Marian was, is she not?
... Yeah, she is.
Then fret not!
Surely all shall be well, I daresay!
... What makes you so sure?
I have roamed across lands aplenty in search of treasure.
Yeah, you just told me that.
Harken, and be silent!
Fine.
Chime calmly resumes her story.
... I have roamed across lands aplenty in search of treasure.
Treasure I knew naught of...
Nay, treasure whose very existence I could scarce be sure of!
... Why?
This is the part where thou shouldst ask me why!
Wait, didn't you just tell me to be quiet and listen?
Use your wits!
An aide ought to be quick on the uptake, y'know!
... Why?
That I cannot recall with certainty.
What I do remember is... the desperation
that I would sooner have met mine end than been undone in my quest for treasure.
So, did you find it?
... Aye, I didst find it.
Chime turns her head slightly,
glancing over her shoulder at Crown, who is talking with Anis and Neon.
... 'Tis most precious;
so precious that I'd gladly lay down mine own worthless little life for it, mark ye.
And mark ye well,
those whom I hold dear...
shall surely hold me dear in return.
Rapi wouldst not wish to part from thee.
She hath her reasons, after all.
Fret not thyself too much.
I, too, am hurrying along the swiftest path I can.
... Okay, got it.
Good. If thou hast understood, go forth and ask of Her Highness whether she doth feel hunger.
Looking at the time,
I realize that about as much time has passed as I walked before the break.
And the moment I notice this, I can feel—and even see—my pace slowing noticeably.
Thanks.
... Hast thou lost thy senses!?
Cease thy nonsense and go ask at once!
... Okay.
After a short break, we set off again.
My steps feel much lighter than before.
A Small Gesture of Thanks
As the sun begins to set,
Chime leads us to an empty house and starts preparing for the night.
Anis, Neon, and I pitch in to help.
Hmm... One try, and thou hast already grown quite the useful little thing, hast thou not?
Place it here, will ye?
On it!
Anis dumps all the tree branches she collected in a heap.
Right here, Miss.
Oh, thank you.
With an air of elegance, Neon sets the table in front of Crown.
Thou hast had a long day.
Rest thee now, for on the morrow we shall depart at early morn.
Got it.
And... thanks. You helped me feel a bit better.
... Go on, finish thy preparations already!
Chime whirls around and starts rummaging through her backpack.
... Chime.
What be it?
Without looking at me,
Chime keeps rummaging through her backpack while answering.
Mind telling me your story while we set up?
Hast not I spoken enough already?
Tsk, tsk... Did it all pass through thine ears and out the other, hmm?
I'd like to hear more.
You were telling me about the Ark earlier, right?
I'd like to hear about your life too...
like what you like and dislike,
things you do during your free time in the kingdom, or if you've had any hard times... you know, stuff like that.
I want to hear more of your stories.
... Huh?
Was that really so surprising?
Why art thou... curious about such things...?
We haven't met for very long, so I want to get to know you better.
Somehow... I have a feeling this won't be the last time we see each other.
... Heh heh!
Thou think'st I would fall for such sweet talk?
Cease thy babbling and come assist me at once!
A few moments later.
Ah, the first time I didst meet Her Highness...
Mm-hm.
I was but a child then...
Foolish, reckless, I was.
Really? Hard to imagine.
Hehe. Thou dost speak thus because thou hast ne'er seen the way I was afore.
Back then...
Heh...!
Chime, who had been telling her story with a gentle smile, suddenly bolts upright.
R-Rapscallion!
What hast thou done to me?!
I just want to hear more of your stories...
Chime? Is there something the matter?
D-don't come this way, Your Highness!
This man doth mean no good...!
Indeed...?
She means he's cooking up some plan.
Oh! Hehe, I was momentarily confused.
Chime, please, compose yourself.
Crown soothes Chime, then sits down in front of me.
Have you spoken with Chime much?
Yeah, I feel really energized thanks to Chime.
Did you get to chat with the two of them a lot, too?
Indeed. I see that even the Advisor is blessed with such exemplary subjects.
... I told you I'm not going to be your advisor.
And they're not my subjects—they're my comrades.
There she goes again, trying to steal him from us!
Hmm… maybe there's something about Master?
Like being born under a certain star sign
and totally irresistible to the opposite sex without even trying, y'know?
... Looks like you might be onto something.
My apologies. Perhaps my lack of preparation led me to misspeak.
Methinks the word is "willingness," Your Highness.
Oh my, I misspoke again.
... But, Your Highness... dost thou truly intend to make this fool thy advisor?
Chime?
'Tis naught!
I-I shall prepare supper forthwith!
During dinner that evening,
Chime and Crown sit side by side, whispering away to each other.
A Precious Gift
The following morning...
Hmph. So, in the end, thou didst refuse outright?
I speak of becoming the kingdom's advisor.
... Yeah, sorry.
... Is that so?
You're not going to try to talk me into it anymore?
I know not what Her Highness thinks.
Yet as for me, such is how I see it.
... Did I not tell thee? Those dear to thee surely hold thee dear as well.
To them, it would seem as though some precious thing hath been taken away.
Have you told Crown what we talked about?
... Mere trifles, I assure thee.
I told her, thou too hast things precious unto thee.
... Uh-huh.
We left our discourse unfinished yesterday.
Pray tell, what is Marian to thee?
Someone incredibly important to me.
She's like family to me.
Is that so?
Chime looks up at the sky in silence.
... It seems thou dost miss her sorely.
Is there some reason keeping thee from meeting her?
... Chime, you're surprisingly calm right now.
I have to admit, I'm a bit impressed.
R-Rapscallion! What dost thou take me for?
And now thou wouldst change the subject?
After standing up and huffing angrily for a while, Chime plops back down.
... Didst thou think I would be shouting all day?
But you were going at it nonstop yesterday...
That's 'cause thou had the nerve to refuse the kingdom's advisor post!
Thou truly art a master at ruffling tempers!
S-sorry...
*Sigh*
Chime lets out a sigh, then begins to prepare to set out again.
Here, let me help.
... I shall deliver thy words.
What?
To Marian, that is.
And I shall convey to her
how dearly thou dost hold her.
Though it seems Marian hath gathered herself in her own fashion,
a little comfort such as this ought to bolster her spirit in these trying times.
Thank you, Chime.
... Thou art welcome.
Soon, we finish preparing to set out.
Chime glances at the bags I've packed and nods in approval.
Not bad.
... As I spake ere now, I had meant to make thee my aide until we reach our destination.
Yet, for thy sake, I shall specially let it end here.
Really? I don't mind doing more.
I need thee not, I daresay!
Good grief, canst thou never leave me be?
Chime grumbles as she gathers her bags.
... I shall give thee a reward.
Oh? What reward?
I shall tell Marian of thee, but...
thou hast not truly heard how she fares,
nor what she hath endured, hast thou?
If it pleases thee, I shall recount it.
There remain yet three full days ere we reach our destination.
... Yes, please, and thank you.
Ha! Then I shall begin with the tale of how Snow White brought Marian to the kingdom.
And so, on the way to Red Hood's hometown,
we share stories of Marian...
and talk about the things that matter most to us.
